mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment that erodes corporate earnings power and investor sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand and construction activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth and HOUST both rise in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth and HOUST both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 1% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >1% MoM for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises by more than 1% month-over-month for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent YoY decline in retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) of 3% or more, combined with a flat or declining industrial production (INDPRO), signals broad-based demand weakness that depresses earnings across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of aggressive monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change <= -3% AND INDPRO flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls by 3% or more YoY and INDPRO is flat or declining, outside of monetary easing periods.
